description:
## Problem
The specification (Clause 6.2) requires source data from DIGen. BenchBox ships no TPC-DI generator. The owner has decided to ship the TPC's tools inside the package so users need only Java.

## Owner decisions (choice dialogs, 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21)
- 2026-11-21, generator: "We will ship any needed assets with BenchBox and include the sourcing and upstream license conditions for our users to review and consider". Clarified the same day: the TPC-DI tools exactly as the TPC distributes them (DIGen, PDGF, dictionaries, configuration), unmodified, inside the BenchBox package, with the TPC licence, the PDGF licence, the legend and a sourcing file; BenchBox runs them with the user's Java; no generator code is ported or rewritten. Source: "The official archive you place at ~/Developer/tpc-tools/, with SHA-256 recorded."
- 2026-11-21, licence acknowledgement: no flag. "print the licence locations and conditions on every generation and continue." (This replaces the earlier `--accept-tpcdi-tools-license` decision.)
- 2026-11-21: "I rule now that publishing BenchBox results is research use."
- For the record, as told to the owner before the decision: the PDGF licence text read from mirrors forbids redistribution and says bankmark let the TPC distribute it "as part of the 'TPC Benchmark DI' only"; the TPC EULA clause 9 allows redistribution of TPC software with its legend and has no carve-out for third-party parts. Shipping is the owner's decision.
- 2026-11-21, comment policy: `external` entries "Approved in advance for the TPC-DI files only, with the soundness review."

## Change
Add one tools directory, `benchbox/_binaries/tpc-di/tools/`, holding the contents of the official `TPC-DI_Tools_v1.1.0.zip` exactly as extracted: DIGen, the PDGF directory with its jars, dictionaries and configuration, and every licence file in the archive. Add beside it `SOURCING.md`: archive name, SHA-256, download location, date obtained, a per-file SHA-256 manifest, the statement that nothing was modified, the full TPC EULA and PDGF licence texts (or their paths in the directory), the PDGF conditions a user should read (use limited to "internal, academic, and research purposes only"; no modification, decompilation or redistribution), and the owner's decision. Mirror the files under `_sources/tpc-di/tools/` only if the TPC-H and TPC-DS convention requires both places; otherwise one place. Package data, MANIFEST.in, `external` policy entries, and the step 6 guard's allowed location. A test compares every shipped file with the manifest.

## Decision gates
Owner action first: the owner places the official `TPC-DI_Tools_v1.1.0.zip` and the separate Appendix archive (specification page 117) under `~/Developer/tpc-tools/`. This item stays blocked until both are there. The archives are never committed as archives. Before opening the pull request, measure the built wheel and report its size before and after in the description. If the wheel would exceed PyPI's per-file limit for the project or grow by more than the owner has seen, stop and ask: the size is a number the owner has not approved. If the pull request would exceed the review bot's limit (about 20,000 changed lines or 300 files) because of text files in the archive, stop and report options; do not split or repack the archive's contents on your own. If the archive contains a file whose own licence text forbids what this step does in words not already shown to the owner (see the record above), quote it in the pull request and stop. Nothing is taken from the Databricks project's copy of the tools.

## Verification rubric
Pass: every file under the tools directory equals the archive member byte for byte (the manifest test, which fails when one byte of a fixture copy is changed); `uv build --wheel && unzip -l dist/benchbox-*.whl | rg 'tpc-di/tools/'` lists DIGen and PDGF; the wheel sizes are in the pull request; SOURCING.md contains both licence texts or their paths and the archive SHA-256; the step 6 guard passes with the tools in their directory and fails when a copy of one jar is placed elsewhere; `make comment-policy-check` and `make pr-preflight` pass; the soundness review of the head is a success.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21)
- The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`.
- Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking. `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job the runner never ran or cancelled, never for a failed test.
- Review threads: reply; resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again.
- Subagents are read-only. No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment.
- Any limit, default, threshold, status token, message or label text the owner has not already chosen (see tpcdi-correction-plan-20261120) is shown to the owner before it is committed.
- A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`. One pull request for this item, merged before the next item starts.
- From the quarantine step until the reopening step, no TPC-DI entry point may produce a result that reads PASSED or is admitted for publication.
- Sources. SQL derived from the Databricks project (`src/incremental_batches/**` at commit 8e0f944, treated as MIT on the owner's instruction) may be committed only after the provenance step has merged, only under `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/`, with every file listed in `PROVENANCE.json` and with all comments removed.
- TPC and bankmark files (DIGen, PDGF, dictionaries, configuration, EULA, appendix SQL) come only from the official archive the owner supplies, are committed unmodified and only in the directories named in the tools step. Never copy from the Databricks project or the DuckDB implementation: their copies of the tools or the tools zip, DIGen output, generated reference files, audit snapshots, their copy or rewrite of the appendix SQL, or any generator code (`src/tools/**`). Never commit DIGen output.
- The specification wins over the Databricks project without asking. Each behaviour of the project that is kept and each change made to follow the specification is one row in `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/DEPARTURES.yaml`, which the owner approves at the milestone stop.
- A difference from the DuckDB implementation (djouallah/tpcdi) that is not in the written list of expected differences is a finding: it is triaged and listed in the pull request before the step is armed.
- Staging files produced by DIGen are never edited. The official audit, validation and visibility SQL is never edited in the repository.
